Today’s hearing will focus on integrating and regulating micromobility options in New York City. IN addition to this oversight topic, we will be hearing two introductions and one resolution. Intro 606, co-sponsored by Council Member Robert Holden, a Local Law in relation to requiring that every bicycle with electric assist, electric scooter and other legal motorized vehicle be licensed and registered. Micromobility devices cover a wide variety of small low-speed, human or electric-powered transportation devices like bicycles, scooters, electric assist bicycles, also known as e-bikes, and electric scooters. Over time, as battery and transportation technology has improved, e-bikes, escooters and other motorized micromobility devices have increasingly appeared on our streets. The Department of Transportation is tasked with regulating these devices and ensuring that our shared streets are safe. On October 11, 2024, Speaker Adams with other elected officials and community leaders called for an operational pause of the expansion into Queens to improve on the pilot through better regulation, enforcement, and safety measures.
